passage: In the school yard in Accra, Kofi walked around the long way so he would not pass Dalia's class. Last Friday he had promised to help her paint the set for the play, but he went to play football instead and never said a word. Now his ears burned whenever he saw her. All week he hid behind the water tank at lunch. On Thursday he saw her holding a heavy board alone, and his stomach turned. He walked across the yard and said, "I did not come because I chose football. I am sorry. Can I paint with you now?" Dalia looked at him for a moment and handed him a brush.

qa.q: Which city is the school in?
Why did Kofi avoid Dalia's class and hide behind the water tank?
qa.a: He was embarrassed and ashamed for breaking his promise to help paint the set.

qa.q: What did Kofi do that started to repair things?
qa.a: He told her the truth, said sorry and offered to paint with her, instead of hiding any longer.

qa.q: How might Dalia have felt when Kofi finally came over?
qa.a: Dalia may have felt let down earlier and cautious, but she seemed willing to accept the honest apology, since she handed him a brush.

grounding: A child ashamed of breaking his promise hides for a week, then tells his friend the truth, apologises and offers to make it up.
